name: Splitseam Wool-Analog Tube Socks
description: Thick-ribbed tube socks in a mottled grey-black, hand-darned at the heel with a different-colored thread — someone used whatever orange yarn they had. The elastic at the cuff is shot on one sock, so it sags mid-calf. Warm enough for a Shelf winter if you layer two pairs.
functionality: Thick rib provides insulation against concrete floors and sub-zero winters; darned heel extends lifespan.
what_it_says: These are kept, not bought — someone thought they were worth repairing.
story_hooks: The orange darning thread is the exact shade used by a specific Shelf gang as a color marker — wearing these in the wrong block is a mistake.
Sold in pairs at the Ruck Market, they sometimes come with the previous owner's name scratched into the sole with a pin.

physical_description.visual_profile: Chunky, utilitarian tube socks with a distinctly hand-made quality. They sit mid-calf when elastic functions properly, slouching lower on one foot. The mottled grey-black colorway reads as practical streetwear, suggesting multiple wears and minimal care. The bright orange darning patch at the heel is a bold, unintentional accent that signals resourcefulness over fashion.
physical_description.fit: Loose, slouching tube fit. One sock maintains mid-calf height; the other sags toward the ankle due to degraded elastic. Designed for layering and bulk rather than form-fitting.
physical_description.primary_material: Wool-analog blend (likely recycled synth-wool or treated natural fiber), hand-darned with contrasting orange yarn at stress points
physical_description.texture: Thick ribbed knit with a slightly weathered, nubby surface. The darn is rougher, more visible, creating tactile contrast. Elasticized cuff area shows fraying and loss of tension.
physical_description.color_scheme: Mottled grey-black base with a striking bright orange repair darn at the heel. No pattern except the hand-worked darning.
physical_description.closures: Elasticized cuff — degraded on one sock, still functional on the other
distinctive_features: Hand-darned orange heel repair (visible, unmatched thread)
One sock with failing elastic, creating deliberate slouch
Thick ribbed construction for durability and warmth
Mottled coloring suggesting age or low-quality dye lot
Evidence of multiple repairs or patch attempts
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 4-5 functional/salvage. These are survival wear, not fashion.
physical_description.cultural_context: Street-tier, sub-grade. Worn by people in the Shelf or industrial zones who repair what they have rather than replace it. No corporate branding, no aug-integration. Pure necessity.
physical_description.condition_typical: Weathered, patched, one-of-a-kind. These look like they've been through winters. The orange darn is a badge of prolonged use.
